Definition: to duplicate or repeat; by implication, to protest, testify (as by reiteration); intensively, to encompass, restore (as a sort of reduplication)
BiblicalUsage: The word ʻûwd is the Bible's way of saying to testify, to witness, to warn. In Genesis 43:3, The man did solemnly protest unto us. The word turns up 40 times, and each time it points to the same reality.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a witness is not believed for being loud but for telling what was seen, and I will tell what God has done. That is why I come back to ʻûwd whenever I need to remember what is true.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
